title: What annuity training do insurance producers need under the NAIC best interest rule?
description: NAIC Model #275 annuity training: the one-time 4 credit course, insurer product training, the 2020 refresher rule, and California and Texas hour rules.
shortAnswer: Under the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation (#275), as revised in 2020, a producer must complete a one-time 4 credit annuity course before selling annuities and must also meet the insurer's product-specific training standards. The insurer must verify the course before letting the producer sell. States adopt the model individually, and some add more: California requires 8 hours before soliciting and 4 hours every renewal.
keyTakeaways: Model #275 Section 7B(1)(a) requires a one-time 4 credit annuity training course, approved by the state insurance department, before a producer engages in annuity sales.

Section 7A adds a separate duty: a producer may not solicit an annuity without adequate product knowledge and compliance with the insurer's product training standards, which insurers must supply under Section 6C(2)(c).

The 2020 best interest revision required producers who had taken the earlier course to complete a new 4 credit course or a 1 credit update within 6 months of their state's effective date (Section 7B(6)).
Insurers must verify completion before a producer sells their annuities (Section 7B(11)) and run a supervision system that is tested and reported to senior management every year.

State rules can exceed the model: California Insurance Code section 1749.8 requires 8 hours initially plus 4 hours before each renewal, and Texas requires a 4 hour certification course plus 8 hours of annuity CE every 2 years.
jurisdiction: United States (state insurance regulation; NAIC Model #275 as adopted by each state, with California and Texas as verified examples)
regulator: State insurance departments, including the California Department of Insurance and the Texas Department of Insurance (TDI), adopting model rules developed by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)
appliesTo: Licensed life insurance producers who sell, solicit or recommend annuities
Insurers that issue annuities, for product training, verification and supervision duties
General agencies and independent agencies that supervise producers under contract with insurers
Continuing education providers offering state-approved annuity courses

sections.heading: What training does NAIC Model #275 require before a producer sells annuities?

blocks.text: Model #275 requires two kinds of training: a generic, state-approved annuity course of at least 4 continuing education credits, and the insurer's own product-specific training. Both must be in place before the producer recommends or sells an annuity. The text referred to on this page is the Spring 2020 edition of the [Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation](https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/model-law-275.pdf), which replaced the earlier suitability standard with a best interest standard, as at November 2026.

blocks.title: Model #275, Section 7B(1)(a)
blocks.text: "A producer who engages in the sale of annuity products shall complete a one-time four (4) credit training course approved by the department of insurance and provided by the department of insurance-approved education provider."

Timing depends on when the producer was licensed. Under Section 7B(1)(b), a producer who already held a life insurance line of authority when the state adopted the regulation had 6 months to complete the course. Anyone who obtains a life line of authority on or after the effective date may not sell annuities at all until the course is done. Section 7B(2) sets the course length as sufficient to qualify for at least 4 CE credits, and allows longer courses.

The model is not law until a state adopts it, so the effective date, the wording and any extra requirements come from each state's insurance department. General producer CE hours, which the annuity course usually counts toward, are covered on the page on [insurance producer continuing education requirements](/regulations/insurance-producer-continuing-education-requirements).

sections.heading: What must the 4 credit annuity course cover?

blocks.text: The course must cover six topics fixed by Section 7B(3), and it must stay generic. Providers may not use it to market products or teach sales technique, which separates it clearly from insurer product training.

items: The types of annuities and the various classifications of annuities.
Identification of the parties to an annuity.
How product-specific annuity contract features affect consumers.
The application of income taxation to qualified and non-qualified annuities.
The appropriate standard of conduct, sales practices, replacement and disclosure requirements.

blocks.text: Section 7B(4) requires providers to cover every listed topic and bars them from presenting marketing information, training on sales techniques, or specific information about a particular insurer's products. Section 7B(5) requires the provider to register as a CE provider in the state, and Section 7B(7) allows classroom or self-study delivery under the state's CE rules. Section 7B(8) requires providers to report completions and issue certificates.

sections.heading: What product-specific training must insurers provide?

blocks.text: Every insurer that issues annuities must give its producers training and materials explaining all material features of its annuity products, and must set standards for that training. The generic course alone does not authorize a producer to sell a particular contract.

Section 7A states that a producer "shall not solicit the sale of an annuity product unless the producer has adequate knowledge of the product to recommend the annuity and the producer is in compliance with the insurer's standards for product training." The producer may rely on insurer-provided standards and materials to meet that duty. On the insurer side, Section 6C(2) makes the training part of the supervision system: the insurer must inform producers of the regulation and build it into relevant training manuals (6C(2)(a)), establish standards for product training and procedures requiring producers to comply with Section 7 (6C(2)(b)), and provide product-specific training and materials (6C(2)(c)).

In practice this means a producer appointed with several insurers carries one generic course record and a separate product training record per insurer and per product. A [training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) that lists products as rows, rather than only courses, makes gaps visible when a new contract or rider is launched.

sections.heading: What changed with the 2020 best interest revision?

blocks.text: The 2020 revision raised the conduct standard from suitability to best interest and required a one-time refresher for producers trained under the old rule. Section 7B(6) gave those producers 6 months after the amended regulation's effective date to complete either a new 4 credit course approved after that date, or a one-time 1 credit course on sales practices, replacement and disclosure under the amended rule.

The conduct content the refresher had to teach is in Section 6A. A producer acts in the consumer's best interest by meeting four obligations: care, disclosure, conflict of interest, and documentation. The care obligation requires the producer to know the consumer's financial situation, insurance needs and financial objectives, to understand the available options, to have a reasonable basis to believe the recommendation addresses those needs over the life of the product, and to communicate the basis for it (Section 6A(1)(a)). Section 6A(1)(d) states that these requirements do not create a fiduciary obligation.

Replacements need specific attention in training. Section 6A(1)(j) requires the producer to consider whether the consumer will incur a surrender charge or lose existing benefits, whether the replacing product would substantially benefit the consumer, and whether the consumer has had another exchange or replacement, in particular within the preceding 60 months. The disclosure obligation in Section 6A(2) requires a form substantially similar to Appendix A, stating which product types the producer is licensed and authorized to sell.

sections.heading: How must insurers verify and supervise annuity training?

blocks.text: The insurer must confirm that a producer has completed the annuity course before allowing them to sell its annuities, and it remains responsible for compliance even when the error is the producer's. Section 7B(11) lets the insurer satisfy verification by obtaining certificates of completion or by relying on reports from commissioner-sponsored database systems or a reasonably reliable commercial database vendor with a reporting arrangement with approved providers.

Section 6C(2)(i) requires the insurer to give senior management, including the senior manager responsible for audit functions, an annual written report on a review, with appropriate testing, of whether the supervision system is effective, the exceptions found and corrective action. Section 8A makes the insurer responsible for compliance and lets the commissioner order corrective action for harmed consumers by the insurer, a general agency, an independent agency or the producer.

Section 9A requires insurers, agencies and producers to keep records of the information used in recommendations for a number of years the state sets; the drafting note suggests that for some states this may be 5 years. The [guide to preparing training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit) covers how to package that evidence.

sections.heading: How do California and Texas go beyond the model?

blocks.text: Both states require more hours than the model and require recurring annuity training, not only a one-time course. Producers licensed in several states should therefore track the strictest applicable requirement, while noting that Model #275 Section 7B(9) treats substantially similar training completed in another state as satisfying the course requirement.

items: **California:** [Insurance Code section 1749.8](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=INS&sectionNum=1749.8) requires every life agent who sells annuities to complete 8 hours of training before soliciting individual consumers, and 4 hours before each license renewal. The 8 hour course does not satisfy the 4 hour renewal requirement. Topics include California annuity law, prohibited sales practices, recognizing indicators that a prospective insured may lack the short-term memory or judgment to knowingly buy, and fraudulent and unfair trade practices. Content primarily intended to promote sales does not qualify.

**Texas:** [28 Texas Administrative Code section 19.1028](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/28-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-19-1028) bars a resident agent licensed or renewed on or after April 1, 2010 from selling annuities until they complete an annuity certification course of at least 4 hours, covering Insurance Code Chapters 1114 and 1115, the prohibitions in sections 541.051 to 541.061, indicators of diminished capacity, and practices prohibited by Penal Code Chapter 35. Proof must be kept for 4 years. [Section 19.1029](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/28-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-19-1029) then requires at least 8 hours of TDI-certified annuity CE in each 2 year licensing period, with the certification course counting as 4 of those hours in the period it is taken.

sections.heading: What evidence should a producer and an insurer hold?

blocks.text: Each obligation in the model falls on a different party and produces a different record. The table maps them so that a market conduct examiner's request can be answered from one place.

blocks.text: For producers who also hold securities registrations, note that the model's Section 6E provides a safe harbor for recommendations made in compliance with comparable standards, but it does not remove the training duties in Section 7. Separate securities CE is covered on the page on [FINRA continuing education requirements](/regulations/finra-continuing-education-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models the generic annuity outline, each insurer's product features and each state's extra hour rules as separate obligations, each linked to the roles and products it covers. When a product or rider changes, the affected learning outcomes and producers are identified from the framework, so verification evidence stays current without rebuilding courses.

faqs.q: Does the 4 credit annuity course count toward general continuing education?
faqs.a: Usually yes, but it depends on the state. The model routes the course through the state's CE approval rules, and California and Texas both let the annuity hours count toward the licensee's overall CE requirement while still requiring the specific annuity hours to be completed.

faqs.q: Can a producer rely on another state's annuity course?
faqs.a: Under Model #275 Section 7B(9), completing substantially similar training requirements in another state is deemed to satisfy the course requirement. Section 7B(10) extends this to courses with substantially similar components. Each state's adopted text should be checked, because some states impose additional state-specific hours.

faqs.q: Is insurer product training the same as the 4 credit course?
faqs.a: No. The 4 credit course must be generic and may not include marketing, sales techniques or a particular insurer's products. Product-specific training is a separate duty under Section 7A and Section 6C(2)(c), delivered or specified by each insurer for its own contracts.

faqs.q: Does the best interest standard make producers fiduciaries?
faqs.a: No. Section 6A(1)(d) of Model #275 states that the care obligation does not create a fiduciary obligation or relationship and only creates a regulatory obligation. A fiduciary duty may arise separately under an advisory or financial planning agreement, as Section 6A(1)(i) notes.
